therapeutic_hypothesis.claimed_target: L-type calcium channels (verapamil) + automated insulin delivery (HCL)
therapeutic_hypothesis.proposed_mechanism: Calcium channel blockade to preserve beta cell function + automated glucose control
therapeutic_hypothesis.intended_biology: Beta cell preservation and improved glycemic control in new onset Type 1 diabetes
therapeutic_hypothesis.target_population: Patients with new onset Type 1 diabetes
therapeutic_hypothesis.primary_endpoint: C-peptide Area Under the Curve (AUC) at 52 weeks

results.effect_size: Verapamil vs placebo: Mean Difference 0.14 (95% CI: 0.01-0.27), p = 0.04; HCL vs non-HCL: Mean Difference -0.01 (95% CI: -0.11-0.10), p = 0.89
biomarker_changes: C-peptide AUC at 52 weeks: Verapamil 0.65 vs Placebo 0.44 (pmol/ml)*minutes
Peak C-peptide at 52 weeks: Verapamil 0.83 vs Placebo 0.55 pmol/mL
subgroup_findings: HCL showed superior glycemic control: Mean glucose 145 vs 167 mg/dL (p<0.001)
HCL achieved 78% vs 64% time in range 70-180 mg/dL (p<0.001)
More participants with HCL achieved HbA1c <7.0%: 42 vs 26
results.dose_information: Verapamil 120mg tablet daily; HCL automated insulin delivery system
